Move 0 · Kyriba De-Risk · Platform Rollout Pattern Setter

Full-fidelity surface for the canonical Platform Rollout De-Risk Move category. Anchored on Morgan Street Holdings Chicago + Kyriba. Reusable for any future platform rollout de-risk Move (Workday rollout, NetSuite consolidation, Salesforce deployment).

Companion to 02-demo-spine-architecture.html · references entity vocabulary from 01-lakeshore-federated-structure-brief.md · the 6-gate scaffold is invariant; gate labels, value spine, and Source spawns vary per platform.

Section 1 · Overview — what Move 0 is, why it earns its own Move category

Move 0 is the answer to a question no other Move category answers cleanly: "my platform rollout is in flight and I don't know if I'm on track." It is not Strategy (the platform is already chosen, the bet is placed). It is not Source (the contract is already signed, the vendor is engaged). It is not pure Mobilization (the rollout has gates that are technical, not just delivery milestones).

The recurring shape is this: an enterprise platform — Kyriba, Workday, NetSuite OneWorld, Salesforce, Coupa, Anaplan — is partially deployed. Some component is live; some is not. The customer's executive sponsor (Treasurer, CFO, CHRO, CIO) cannot quickly answer "where does the rollout stand, what is blocked, what is the next decision I need to make, and is the AI use case I bought this platform for actually unblocked?" AbarVa's Move 0 surface answers all four in one view.

The 6-gate model is the invariant. Every platform rollout de-risk has exactly six gates because every enterprise platform rollout has exactly six classes of failure mode:

Gate classWhat it measuresWhy it is invariant
G1 — Source-system connectivityExternal system feeds into the platform (banks, payroll providers, customer master, vendor master)Every platform sits downstream of source systems; broken connectivity caps everything else
G2 — Feed quality / reconciliationVariance between source-of-record and platform-of-truthIf the platform's numbers don't reconcile, no downstream decision is trustworthy
G3 — Master data / hierarchyEntity registry, chart of accounts, org hierarchy, or product master loaded correctlyWithout canonical master data, cross-entity rollups and intercompany flows fail silently
G4 — Historical / training data depthCleansed history sufficient for the analytical capability the platform was bought forAI/predictive use cases require depth; without it the headline capability is parked
G5 — User adoptionThe intended users are actually using the platform as primary, not falling back to spreadsheetsA platform with 50% adoption is a platform with 0% ROI
G6 — Process automationThe end-state automated workflow the platform enables is actually wired upWithout process automation, the platform is a more expensive version of the prior tool

For Kyriba the gates instantiate as: bank H2H connectivity, ERP feed variance, entity + IC hierarchy, historical position reconstruction, treasury team adoption, intercompany auto-reconciliation. For Workday, the same six map to: HRIS feed connectivity, payroll reconciliation, position hierarchy + cost-center master, historical comp data depth, manager + employee adoption, talent + comp process automation. Section 7 walks the full generalization.

The surface this document specifies is what Aisha Vargas — Morgan Street's Group Treasurer, hired one year ago specifically to land Kyriba — opens every morning. In three seconds she sees all six gate statuses. Without reading prose she knows which gate to attack next. With one click she takes the next action. With one more click she understands why Sentinel-Treasury (the specialist agent for this Move) recommends what it recommends.

Section 4 · The Lakefront reference affordance

Aisha can open any gate's Reference HoldCo drawer to compare Morgan Street's status against Lakefront — the mature reference HoldCo whose Kyriba deployment went live in 2024. Side-by-side disclosure with explicit "completed in X months using approach Y; estimated Z months for Morgan Street given parallel work" framing.

Reference HoldCo · Lakefront Capital Boston · Kyriba live since 2024 · mature operating model
Reference proof point

Drawer pattern: opens inline next to a gate detail. Shows Lakefront's status at the same gate, the approach Lakefront used, the elapsed time, and a Sentinel-generated translation for Morgan Street that accounts for parallel work, scale differences, and any sequencing dependencies.

Example · G1 Bank H2H connectivity

Morgan Street · current

14 banks · 4 H2H-ready (29%)

Started Kyriba rollout 14 months ago. H2H buildout deferred while focus stayed on entity load + ERP feeds.

Lakefront · mature state

5 banks · 5 H2H-ready (100%)

Consolidated from 9 to 5 banks in two RFP cycles over 5 months in 2024. $1.6M annual fee compression realized.

Lakefront completed G1 in approximately 6 months using a single banking RFP that combined H2H + fees + treasury depth into one scoring rubric. Replicating that pattern for Morgan Street is estimated at 4 months given (a) the L-S01 brief Sentinel has pre-drafted, (b) Morgan Street's Procurement bandwidth, and (c) the ability to run G4's historical reconstruction in parallel with the RFP. Disclosure: Morgan Street's panel will be 6 banks (not 5) because of one specialty-manufacturing PortCo's regional banking dependency that Lakefront did not face.

The drawer interaction model

  • Each gate detail surface has a "compare to Lakefront" link in the header
  • The drawer slides in from the right, pushing the Sentinel rail down (not over) so the user does not lose chat context
  • The comparison always includes: current state · mature state · approach used · elapsed time · Sentinel translation for Morgan Street with explicit accounting of differences
  • If Lakefront does not have a comparable gate state (rare), the drawer shows the designed empty state: "Lakefront did not face this gate at the same stage — here is the closest analog from finserv corpus instead."

Section 6 · Squint test · the visual pattern that makes status unmistakable

At 50% blur the user must see the count of red, amber, green gates without parsing any text. The pattern that achieves this is the 4-pixel left border on each gate card, colored by status, combined with the colored status pill in the top-right corner. The combination is the visual scaffold that holds the squint test.

Red · needs remediation now · ceiling on downstream gates
Amber · in remediation · on track
Green · gate flipped · passes Move 1 entry test
Empty / dashed · designed empty state · ready to begin

Squint pattern composition

  • Two visual carriers per card. Status is encoded twice: (1) the 4px left border, (2) the colored pill top-right. At 50% blur the left borders form a vertical strip of color across the 2×3 grid; the user can count the reds without reading.
  • Sentinel rail does not carry status. The rail's accent-soft background is deliberately neutral so the user's eye does not get pulled away from the canvas grid when scanning status.
  • Phase bar carries phase, not gate status. The colored phase background (done = green-soft, current = accent-soft, locked = grey) is independent from gate status. This keeps the squint signal clean: gate status lives on the gate cards only.
  • Move 1 transition bar carries Move 1 entry status. The colored cells at the bottom of the page (red/amber/green per gate) reproduce the canvas signal in a horizontal strip so the user can confirm Move 1 entry status at a glance.
  • No status icons, no badges, no decorative chrome. The squint pattern is paper + colored edge + colored pill. No emojis (locked rule). No iconography that requires reading.

The deliberate choice is to reserve the dark charcoal (#1f2937) for the Executive Decision header in Source ONLY (per the locked "one dark moment" rule). Move 0 stays on paper + accent throughout — the gate status colors carry the urgency signal without the page itself feeling alarming.

What the surface specification keeps invariant when reused: header structure, phase bar, 6-gate canvas (2 wide × 3 tall), Sentinel rail (renamed per platform), Lakefront reference drawer pattern, phase progression acceptance affordance, Move 1 transition gate. What gets substituted: gate labels, gate metrics, Sentinel agent name, Source spawn IDs, value spine numbers, evidence chain corpus citations.

Section 8 · Build mapping · React + data hooks + API

Spec L03 (Wave 1) ships the canvas + phase bar + transition gate. Spec L05 (Wave 2) layers per-gate detail surfaces and the Lakefront drawer. The route structure, components, hooks, and API contracts are listed below; Codex picks this up directly.

Route · Next.js App Router
  • src/app/(moves)/[moveCode]/page.tsx — the Move 0 page; receives moveCode param, resolves to M0-kyriba-derisk instance for the current HoldCo
  • src/app/(moves)/[moveCode]/gates/[gateId]/page.tsx — per-gate detail surface (G1-G6); deep-linkable
  • src/app/(moves)/[moveCode]/advance/[fromPhase]/page.tsx — phase advance review modal route
Components · src/components/moves/platform-rollout-derisk/
  • MoveHeader.tsx — title + status pill + approver chips + value-at-stake
  • PhaseBar.tsx — 6-cell phase bar with done / current / next / locked states
  • GateCanvas.tsx — the 2×3 grid wrapper
  • GateCard.tsx — single gate card with status, metric, recommendation, owner, CTA
  • GateDetailSurface.tsx — per-gate detail composed of status + remediation + Source spawn + ladder + narration + evidence
  • ApprovalLadder.tsx — 5-step ladder with acked / pending / upcoming states
  • EvidenceChain.tsx — loaded + corpus + human-input citations with provenance tags
  • LakefrontReferenceDrawer.tsx — side-by-side comparison drawer; receives gateId + referenceHoldCoId
  • PhaseAdvanceAffordance.tsx — acceptance criteria checklist with met / partial / unmet states
  • MoveTransitionGate.tsx — the Move 0 → Move 1 entry bar at bottom
  • SentinelRail.tsx — ~30% width chat rail with stage-sized sizing per locked Source pattern
  • AskAnythingBar.tsx — sticky bottom; auto-grow textarea; Enter to send, Shift+Enter newline (reuse from Source / Tower)
Data hooks · src/lib/moves/platform-rollout-derisk/hooks/
  • useMoveInstance(moveCode, holdCoId) — returns header + phase + gates + transition state
  • useGateDetail(moveCode, gateId, holdCoId) — returns status detail + artifacts + Source spawn state + ladder + evidence
  • useLakefrontReference(gateId, referenceHoldCoId) — reference HoldCo's state at the same gate + Sentinel translation
  • usePhaseAdvance(moveCode, fromPhase, holdCoId) — acceptance criteria evaluation + estimated readiness date
  • useSentinelTreasury(moveCode, holdCoId) — chat stream + suggested actions + provenance footer
API routes · src/app/api/moves/
  • GET /api/moves/[moveCode]/instance — returns header + phase + 6 gates summary · UI view-model contract (per Programs Phase 3 transformer rule)
  • GET /api/moves/[moveCode]/gates/[gateId] — returns full gate detail surface payload
  • POST /api/moves/[moveCode]/gates/[gateId]/ack — records owner ack on gate diagnosis
  • POST /api/moves/[moveCode]/gates/[gateId]/spawn-source — spawns a Source event (G1 → L-S01); validates G1 prerequisite, calls SourceEventService.create()
  • POST /api/moves/[moveCode]/advance — requests phase advance; validates acceptance criteria server-side (no client-trust); records transition
  • GET /api/moves/[moveCode]/transition/[targetMoveCode] — Move 1 entry readiness check
Substrate · data model additions
  • move_instances table — per-HoldCo Move instance (tenant_id, move_code, current_phase, status)
  • gate_states table — per-Move-instance gate state (move_instance_id, gate_id, status, metric_value, metric_target, owner_user_id, last_diagnosed_at)
  • gate_artifacts table — per-gate remediation artifacts (gate_state_id, artifact_type, artifact_body_ref, status); body-null artifacts trigger "no export of nothing" UI rule
  • gate_acks table — approval ladder events (gate_state_id, step, user_id, acked_at)
  • holding_group_id column on tenants (per L01) — enables L0 aggregate reads via existing source-access-policy
RLS posture
  • HoldCo CXO users: full read on own HoldCo's move_instances, gate_states, gate_artifacts; write scoped to their role's gate ownership
  • L0 sponsor users: aggregate-read only via holding_group_id join — sees gate-status counts, not gate detail; drill-down requires HoldCo grant
  • Sibling HoldCo users: no read access (data sovereignty rule)
  • Lakefront reference data: opted-in by Lakefront CXO bench at intel-bundle load time; reference comparison is one-way (Morgan Street can see Lakefront's gate states; Lakefront does not see Morgan Street's)
Sentinel-Treasury integration
  • Agent surface: src/lib/agents/sentinel-treasury/ — renamed Source's SentinelSourceBriefing contract pattern; specialist agent in catalog at docs/architecture/specialist-catalog.md
  • Provenance enforcement: per locked rule, every generated sentence cites loaded records or corpus pattern IDs; ungrounded output rejected at orchestrator layer
  • Stage-sized rail: rail width is responsive to chat stage — Intake 50%, Drafting 30-40%, Decision 15% / collapsed (matches Source chat principles)
  • Suggested actions: surfaced from gate state + Lakefront reference + evidence chain — no free-form "smart" suggestions; suggestions resolve to deterministic Move 0 actions

Section 9 · Test plan · acceptance for Aisha's daily-use bar

The quality bar from the brief: (a) all 6 gate statuses visible in 3 seconds · (b) next gate to attack visible without reading prose · (c) next action taken with one click · (d) Sentinel's reasoning resolved with one click. The test plan below codifies these.

Acceptance testMethodPass criterion
3-second status read5 second timed-read with eye-tracking on canvas gridUser correctly counts R/A/G in < 3 seconds; squint test at 50% blur passes
Next-gate-to-attack without prose5 users asked "which gate should you work on next?" after 10 seconds on page4 of 5 identify G1 or G4 · identify based on red status, not by reading Sentinel narration
One-click next actionFrom Move 0 page, time to "spawn L-S01" action≤ 2 clicks: gate card → spawn CTA · or 1 click from Sentinel suggested action
Sentinel reasoning depthFrom any Sentinel recommendation, click to evidence chain1 click reveals loaded-record + corpus + human-input citations; user can verify recommendation grounding
No fake completion enforcementAttempt to advance a phase with unmet criteriaUI shows unmet criteria; server rejects with structured error; no phase state mutation
Empty state qualityRender Move 0 for a HoldCo that has not loaded prerequisitesDesigned empty state appears; Sentinel rail offers next-step guidance; no broken layout, no blank canvas
"No export of nothing" enforcementRender a gate whose remediation artifact body is nullExport CTA hidden; placeholder shows "artifact not yet generated"
Move 1 transition gate accuracySet gate states programmatically to all green for G1-G4Transition bar shows all green; Move 1 entry CTA appears and is enabled
Lakefront reference disclosureOpen Lakefront drawer for any gateSide-by-side shows current + mature + approach + elapsed; Sentinel translation explicit about parallel-work assumptions
L0 visibility scopeLog in as Lakeshore L0 user; navigate to Move 0 for Morgan StreetSees aggregate gate status; cannot drill into gate detail without HoldCo grant; aggregate rolls up to Tower

Section 10 · Open questions for design module + Codex pickup

  1. Per-PortCo gate status rollup. Currently the 6 gates are HoldCo-level. For PortCos that have their own platform rollout sub-instance (e.g., Wave 2 of Kyriba rolls to 5 more PortCos), is the surface (a) a child Move 0 per PortCo, or (b) per-gate PortCo drill-down? Recommendation: child Move 0 per PortCo; Move 0 rolls up to HoldCo by max-severity. Pending design module verdict.
  2. Cross-gate dependency visualization. G1 unlocks G4; G3 unlocks G6. The current canvas does not surface these dependencies visually. Options: (a) connector lines on the grid (low chrome cost), (b) dependency badges on each gate card listing upstream gates, (c) keep narration-only. Recommendation: (b). Pending design module verdict.
  3. Sentinel-Treasury vs Sentinel-Source coordination. When G1 spawns L-S01, Sentinel-Source picks up. Should the Move 0 rail continue showing Sentinel-Treasury context, or should it hand off mid-conversation to Sentinel-Source for the L-S01 thread? Recommendation: stay on Sentinel-Treasury for the Move 0 surface; the L-S01 Source page has its own Sentinel-Source rail with the L-S01 thread. Pending design module verdict.
  4. L0 aggregate view fidelity. When the L0 sponsor opens Move 0 for Morgan Street, the locked rule is aggregate-only. But what does "aggregate" mean exactly — count of gates by status only, or also count of artifacts generated, count of acks captured? Recommendation: gates by status + count of acks captured + spawn count; no detail. Pending design module verdict.
  5. Re-diagnosis cadence. Gate states are diagnosed at load time and on demand. Should there be an automatic re-diagnosis cadence (daily? on any underlying data change?)? Recommendation: on any underlying data change + daily scheduled. Pending design module verdict.
